'''Ernst Witt''' (26 June 1911 – 3 July 1991) was a German [[mathematician]], one of the leading [[algebra]]ists of his time.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Kersten | first1=Ina | author1-link = Ina Kersten | title=Ernst Witt 1911-1991 | journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung | volume=95 | date=20 October 1993 | pages=166–180 | url=https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/jb_dmv/JB_DMV_095_4.pdf}}</ref>

==Biography==
Witt was born on the island of [[Als (island)|Alsen]], then a part of the [[German Empire]]. Shortly after his birth, his parents moved the family to China to work as missionaries,<ref name="nine">{{cite book |last1=Segal |first1=Sanford L. |title=Mathematicians under the Nazis |date=23 November 2014 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-16463-2 |page=451 |language=en}}</ref> and he did not return to Europe until he was nine.<ref name="nine"/>

After his schooling, Witt went to the [[University of Freiburg]] and the [[University of Göttingen]]. He joined the [[Nazi Party|NSDAP]] (Nazi Party) and was an active party member.<ref>According to Schappacher (letter in Mathematical Intelligencer 1996) it was most certainly him and not [[Oswald Teichmüller]], who attended [[Emmy Noether]]'s private seminar held in her house while wearing his [[Sturmabteilung|SA]]-uniform.</ref> Witt was awarded a [[Ph.D.]] at the University of Göttingen in 1933 with a thesis titled: "Riemann-Roch theorem and zeta-Function in hypercomplexes"<ref name="habil"/> (Riemann-Rochscher Satz und Zeta-Funktion im Hyperkomplexen) that was supervised by [[Gustav Herglotz]], with [[Emmy Noether]] suggesting the topic for the doctorate.<ref name="witter">{{cite book |last1=Frei |first1=Günther |author-link=Günther Frei |title=Emil Artin and Helmut Hasse: The Correspondence 1923-1958 |last2=Lemmermeyer |first2=Franz |last3=Roquette |first3=Peter J. |author-link3=Peter Roquette |date=16 January 2014 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-0348-0715-9 |series=Contributions in Mathematical and Computational Sciences |volume=5 |location=Göttingen |page=439 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-0715-9}}</ref>  He became a qualified lecturer and gave guest lectures in Göttingen and [[University of Hamburg|Hamburg]].<ref name="witter"/> He was also associated with the team led by [[Helmut Hasse]] who led his habilitation. In June 1936, he gave his habilitation lecture.<ref name="habil">{{cite book |last1=Kersten |first1=Ina |editor1-last=Bayer-Fluckiger |editor1-first=Eva |editor2-last=Lewis |editor2-first=David |editor3-last=Ranicki |editor3-first=Andrew |title=Quadratic Forms and Their Applications, Proceedings of the Conference on Quadratic Forms and Their Applications |date=July 1999 |publisher=University College Dublin |page=155 |url=https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~aar/books/dublin.pdf |language=en |chapter=Biography of Ernst Witt (1911{1991)}}</ref>

During [[World War II]] he joined a group of five mathematicians, recruited by [[Wilhelm Fenner]], and which included [[Georg Aumann]], [[Alexander Aigner]], [[Oswald Teichmüller]], Johann Friedrich Schultze and their leader professor [[Wolfgang Franz (mathematician)|Wolfgang Franz]], to form the backbone of the new mathematical research department in the late 1930s that would eventually be called: Section IVc of [[Cipher Department of the High Command of the Wehrmacht]] (abbr. OKW/Chi).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B7sNVKDp-yiJNjE4YTIyOTctNGFlZi00NTliLWEwZWUtOGYxYzEyMjk1NGE1/view|title=Army Security Agency: DF-187 The Career of Wilhelm Fenner with Special Regard to his activity in the field of Cryptography and Cryptanalysis (PDF) |page = 7|date=1 December 1949 |website=Google Drive |access-date=30 March 2016}}</ref><ref>TICOM reports DF-187 A-G and DF-176, ‘European Axis Signal Intelligence in World War II’ vol 2</ref>

From 1937 until 1979, he taught at the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Frei |first1=Günther |last2=Lemmermeyer |first2=Franz |last3=Roquette |first3=Peter J. |title=Emil Artin and Helmut Hasse: The Correspondence 1923-1958 |date=16 January 2014 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |location=Gottigen |isbn=978-3-0348-0715-9 |page=439 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6rDBBAAAQBAJ |language=en}}</ref> He died in Hamburg in 1991, shortly after his 80th birthday.

==Work==
Witt's work has been highly influential. His invention of the [[Witt vector]]s clarifies and generalizes the structure of the [[p-adic number|''p''-adic numbers]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Rabinoff|first=Joseph |author-link=|date=2014|title=The Theory of Witt Vectors|eprint=1409.7445 |class=math.NT}}</ref> It has become fundamental to [[p-adic Hodge theory|''p''-adic Hodge theory]]. 

Witt was the founder of the theory of [[quadratic form]]s over an arbitrary [[Field (mathematics)|field]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Szymiczek |first1=K. |editor1-last=Hazewinkel |editor1-first=M. |editor-link=Michiel Hazewinkel |title=Handbook of Algebra |date=8 July 2009 |publisher=Elsevier |location=Oxford |isbn=978-0-08-093281-1 |page=70 |language=en |chapter=Quadratic Forms|volume=6}}</ref> He [[mathematical proof|proved]] several of the key results, including the [[Witt's theorem|Witt cancellation theorem]]. He defined the [[Witt group#Ring structure|Witt ring]] of all quadratic forms over a field, now a central object in the theory.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Friedlander |first1=Eric |author-link=Eric Friedlander |last2=Grayson |first2=Daniel R. |title=Handbook of K-Theory |date=18 July 2005 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |location=Berlin |isbn=978-3-540-23019-9 |pages=539–577 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Xxg3L20qMeUC |language=en}}</ref>

The [[Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem]] is basic to the study of [[Lie algebra]]s. In [[algebraic geometry]], the [[Hasse–Witt matrix]] of an [[algebraic curve]] over a [[finite field]] determines the cyclic [[étale morphism|étale]] coverings of degree ''p'' of a curve in [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] ''p''.

In the 1970s, Witt claimed that in 1940 he had discovered what would eventually be named the "[[Leech lattice]]" many years before [[John Leech (mathematician)|John Leech]] discovered it in 1965, but Witt did not publish his discovery and the details of exactly what he did are unclear.{{sfn|Witt|1998|pp=328–329}}<ref>{{cite book |last1=Edixhoven |first1=Bas |last2=Couveignes |first2=Jean-Marc |title=Computational Aspects of Modular Forms and Galois Representations: How One Can Compute in Polynomial Time the Value of Ramanujan's Tau at a Prime (AM-176) |date=20 June 2011 |publisher=Princeton University Press |location=Princeton |isbn=978-0-691-14201-2 |page=46 |language=en}}</ref>
